pages.text:
$(l)Welcome to Chapter 3!$()

Spells in the first two chapters only had one normal node — runes lined up and executed all at once. But complex magic requires $(l)rhythm$(): what to do first, how long to wait, under what conditions to trigger, how many times to repeat.

This chapter introduces three node types: $(9)Wait Node$(), $(9)Condition Node$(), $(9)Loop Node$().

pages.title: Extinguish
pages.text:
$(l)Node Structure:$()
Sequence Root Node
├─ $(9)Normal Node$(): $(9)Self VisionCoordinate Copy Copy Water$()
├─ $(9)Wait Node$(): 1 tick
└─ $(9)Normal Node$(): $(9)Dirt Break$()

$(l)Effect:$()Places water at your eye position, waits 1 tick for water to extinguish fire, places dirt to remove water source, then breaks the block.

$(l)Core Knowledge:$()Wait Node makes the spell $(l)pause$() for the specified number of ticks. 1 second = 20 ticks.

pages.title: Extinguish Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

$(l)Wait Node Details$()

$(9)Wait Node$() has only one property: wait time (ticks).

How it works:
·When it's its turn, starts counting down.
·Decrements by 1 each tick.
·When countdown reaches zero, execution completes, sequence proceeds to next node.

$(l)Typical Uses:$()
·Delayed effects: place water first, wait 1 tick before removing water source — water needs time to extinguish.
·Timed triggers: wait 100 ticks (5 seconds) before executing an action.
·Loop synchronization: wait between loop iterations for pulse effects.

To add wait node in editor: right-click magic circle → Add Wait Node → left-click to enter → middle-click to set wait time.

pages.title: Conditional Heal
pages.text:
$(l)Node Structure:$()
Sequence Root Node
├─ $(9)Normal Node$(): $(9)Self CheckHealth 10 <$() (this is rune "<", not garbled text)
└─ $(9)Condition Node$() (condition = true)
　　└─ $(9)Normal Node$(): $(9)Self CheckHealth 20 - Self Heal$()

$(l)Effect:$()First checks if health is below 10, only heals and fills to 20 if true.

$(l)Core Knowledge:$()Condition Node reads the top boolean value from stack, only executes child nodes when boolean matches its preset.

pages.title: Conditional Heal Related Rune Pages
pages.text: These are the runes used in this spell

$(l)Condition Node Details$()

$(9)Condition Node$() has one preset property: $(9)condition$(), which can be set to $(2)true$() or $(4)false$() by $(9)middle-clicking$() the condition node.

How it works:
·Pops boolean from stack top, compares with condition.
·Match → execute child node list until all complete.
·No match → skip child node list.

$(l)Practical Combination:$()
Use comparison runes in normal nodes before condition node to compute conditions:
$(9)Self CheckHealth 10 <$() → stack top becomes $(2)true$() or $(4)false$()
Then condition node decides whether to heal based on this value.

Package the entire check+heal into one spell, and you get $(l)Conditional Healing$().

pages.title: Build Up
pages.text:
$(l)Node Structure:$()
Sequence Root Node
└─ $(9)Loop Node$() (10 times)
　　└─ $(9)Normal Node$(): $(9)Self Copy VisionCoordinate Teleport Self FootCoordinate Dirt$()

$(l)Effect:$()Loops 10 times, each time teleporting yourself to eye position (about 1 block up), then placing dirt beneath your feet. After 10 rounds, a 10-block-high dirt pillar forms.

$(l)Core Knowledge:$()Loop Node repeatedly executes child nodes, number of times determined by $(9)currentTime$().

$(l)Loop Node Details$()

$(9)Loop Node$() has property $(9)currentTime$(), set via $(9)middle-click$():
·Positive → loop fixed number of times, decrement by 1 each round.
·Negative (e.g., -2) → infinite loop until spell interrupted.
·-1 → pop number from stack top as loop count (dynamic loop).

$(l)How does Build Up work?$()
Each iteration: $(9)Self$() pushes player → $(9)Copy$() duplicates player → $(9)VisionCoordinate$() gets eye coordinate → $(9)Teleport$() teleports player to eye coordinate → $(9)Self$() pushes player again → $(9)FootCoordinate$() gets foot coordinate → $(9)Dirt$() places dirt under feet. Results in a 10-block-high dirt pillar.

$(l)Combining the Three Node Types$()

Now you have complete control flow tools:

·$(9)Wait Node$() → controls $(l)rhythm$()
·$(9)Condition Node$() → controls $(l)branching$()
·$(9)Loop Node$() → controls $(l)repetition$()

They can be nested and combined. For example:
·Wait inside loop → interval between iterations
·Condition inside loop → check each iteration whether to continue
·Loop inside condition → only start loop when condition met

$(l)Design your own spells freely!$()
